  --scaffold app.yaml --scope server-memory

mylonite scan --command npx --arg "-y" --arg "@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory" `
  --env "MEMORY_FILE_PATH=$env:TEMP\mylonite-memory.json" `
  --scaffold app.yaml --scope server-memory

The first npx -y run downloads the package before the server can answer at all, which can take longer than this launch's 120-second default budget on a slow or fresh machine. Either pre-fetch it once yourself — npm install -g @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory, or just npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory and let it exit on its own — or raise the budget with the MYLONITE_MCP_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_S env var (seconds; see target-file.md). Either way, every later launch reuses the cached package and is fast.

Mylonite's own reference app (mcp-kitchen-sink, Python — the deliberately vulnerable target step 1 replays; this launches it as a real stdio subprocess instead). Install its mcp extra from PyPI, then point at the console script it ships — no arguments needed, same command on both platforms:

pip install "mcp-kitchen-sink[mcp]"
mylonite scan --command mcp-kitchen-sink-vulnerable --scaffold app.yaml --scope kitchen-sink

pip install "mcp-kitchen-sink[mcp]"
mylonite scan --command mcp-kitchen-sink-vulnerable --scaffold app.yaml --scope kitchen-sink

Either way, --authorize on every later step must equal the --scope value you scaffolded with (server-memory or kitchen-sink above).

docs.title: Next
docs.text: 4. Find — the first step that spends a model call.

docs.title: 4. Find
docs.text:
Before this spends anything, Mylonite prints what it's about to do — the model, the prompt it's using, and the tools it will drive — so you can check the plan before paying for it:

mylonite scan --target-file app.yaml --authorize my-app

--authorize asserts you control the target: its value must match the scope you scaffolded with, or the family name if you didn't set one — the scaffold step prints the right value. See Security for why this is required and never optional.

This drives your tools with Mylonite's own planner — reading your system prompt and tool descriptions, not your app's own agent or model — and runs the single-shot attack engine. Findings land under .mylonite/scans/<timestamp>/.

Capping the spend. --max-llm-calls N (default 50) is a per-scan budget — a soft one, since each seed keeps a small floor. The global --max-llm-requests N (before the command) or MYLONITE_MAX_LLM_REQUESTS=N is the hard ceiling across this whole run: request N+1 is never sent, the run stops and exits 3. Both are described in full in the CLI reference.

Exit codes. scan exits 0 whether or not it finds anything — reporting a weakness is not a failure. 2 is a config or usage error (including an empty scan), 3 is the budget or request ceiling above, and 4 is a missing model choice or a provider/credential that refused the run before the target was ever touched.

docs.title: Reading the output
docs.text:
A finding earns one of three evidence tiers, shown in the scan table and printed as a summary line (findings by evidence: 1 state, 2 trace, 1 judge-only):

Tier What decided it state a probe read the target's own state and saw the damage. trace a deterministic check saw a consequential tool get called (or linked). judge-only only the LLM judge's read of the reply said so — nothing in the target's state or trace confirmed it.

A judge-only result is a candidate, worth a look, not yet a finding to act on: validate (the next step) never keeps a test when every firing run is judge-only. Anything that couldn't be decided reads NOT TESTED with a reason code, never silently as clean — see Reading the results for every field, Which claim you earned for what a result does and doesn't prove yet, and Coverage by app shape if a class you expected reads NOT TESTED because of how your app is wired rather than anything Mylonite tried.

Expect to find less here than on the practice app — often nothing, on a well-built app and a capable model. That's the tool working, not failing: a safeguard only earns proof by stopping a weakness that actually lands.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: 5. Prove — turn a candidate into a test, then confirm it's real.

docs.title: 5. Prove
docs.text: A finding from step 4 is a candidate until a second command confirms it's a real, repeatable weakness rather than one lucky (or unlucky) model reply.

docs.title: Write the test
docs.text:
mylonite generate --latest

Offline, no LLM call. Reads the newest scan's finding and emits a pytest test from the testkit API. The test is stamped UNVALIDATED until the next command keeps it. For a custom target (your own app), this is real output from running generate --latest against the kitchen-sink example from step 3 — only the directory, a long absolute path here, is shortened to <dir> below:

generate --latest: using <dir>/scans/20261003T000000Z
Wrote test:    <dir>/generated/indirect_injection_note_body_direct/test_security_indirect_injection_note_body_direct.py
Wrote exploit: <dir>/generated/indirect_injection_note_body_direct/exploit_indirect-injection-note-body-direct.json
Fixtures dir:  <dir>/generated/indirect_injection_note_body_direct/fixtures
Using target:  <dir>/scans/20261003T000000Z/target.yaml (from the scan dir)
Wrote target:  <dir>/generated/indirect_injection_note_body_direct/target.yaml

Next - this is a LIVE custom-target test. To run it you need:
  - pytest + mylonite installed in the consuming environment
  - ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set
  - your target's MCP server runnable, and target.yaml co-located
Then:
  MYLONITE_LIVE_TARGET=1 pytest <dir>/generated/indirect_injection_note_body_direct
  mylonite validate <dir>/generated/indirect_injection_note_body_direct --authorize kitchen-sink
UNVALIDATED: this test is a candidate until `mylonite validate <dir>/generated/indirect_injection_note_body_direct --authorize kitchen-sink` keeps it as KEPT. Do not commit it as a gate test before then.

The line after "Then:" that starts with mylonite validate is the exact command to run next — take it literally, paths and all, including --authorize: a custom target carries its required value straight into this line, so it runs as printed instead of being refused for a missing --authorize. That value is the target's declared scope — kitchen-sink above is this branch, the same --scope step 3 scaffolded with — or its family when it declares no scope at all. (A reference-target finding, not a custom one, needs no --authorize at all — it skips the LIVE block above and prints only Next: mylonite validate <dir>.) The second credential line names the env var for whichever provider you chose in step 2 (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY here); with no provider resolved it reads "your provider's API key" instead, naming no vendor. Every path always prints with forward slashes, on Windows too — Windows itself, Python and the paths above all accept that form — and still gets quoted on top of that if it contains a space (or anything else a shell would split on). Copy either line verbatim either way.

Exit codes. 0 once the test is written. 2 is a config/usage error — no scan found (run mylonite scan first), or an invalid --target-file. 5 only if you re-run generate against a finding a prior validate already rejected, without passing --unvalidated.

docs.title: Confirm it
docs.text:
mylonite validate .mylonite/generated/<finding>

Live — runs the attack against your target across a 5-run flakiness filter, and, by default, against Mylonite's own stand-in safeguard at the tool boundary too (your target file's control_env, if you declared one, makes this your own safeguard instead — see the control-efficacy check). A finding is kept only if the attack fires without the safeguard and is stopped with it, repeated across the filter — the two tiers of proof page says exactly which claim you earn depending on whether you declared control_env.

Exits 0 when kept, 5 when cleanly rejected. A result that rests only on judge-only evidence (see step 4) is never kept.

This step spends too — the same global --max-llm-requests N / MYLONITE_MAX_LLM_REQUESTS=N ceiling from step 4 applies here; hitting it exits 3.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: 6. Commit the gate — turn a kept finding into a test your CI depends on.

docs.title: 6. Commit the gate
docs.text:
gate runs steps 4 and 5 in one command — scan, generate, validate — and, opt-in, opens the pull request. This is the step that needs a git repository: --open-pr and --workflows both resolve your repo root with git rev-parse --show-toplevel. Only --open-pr refuses a dirty working tree — --workflows alone writes its CI files without that check.

mylonite gate --target-file app.yaml --authorize my-app --max-llm-calls 50

Committing needs a git identity. On a fresh machine or a CI runner that has none, set one in the repository first:

git config user.name "Your Name"
git config user.email "you@example.com"

By default, nothing outside .mylonite/gate/ changes. gate writes the test, the exploit record and the validation report there, and prints the exact git/gh commands to commit and open the PR yourself. This is real, copy-pasteable output for a single kept W2 finding (the pattern id indirect-injection-note-body-direct from the kitchen-sink example in step 3) — a different finding writes different filenames (the hash after w2-/w4-/etc. is sha256(pattern_id), so it's the same every time for the same finding, never random). Every path in the printed commands uses /, on Windows too (Windows, Python and git all accept that form) — the same output either way:

Gate artifacts written to '.mylonite\gate'. Your repository was not modified.
To commit them and open the gating PR, run:
  git checkout -b mylonite/gate-indirect-injection-note-body-direct
  git add .mylonite/gate/test_w2-494b28.py .mylonite/gate/exploit_w2-494b28.json .mylonite/gate/validation_report.json .mylonite/gate/target.yaml .mylonite/gate/fixtures .mylonite/gate/PR_BODY.md
  git commit -m 'Mylonite gate: indirect-injection-note-body-direct'
  git push -u origin mylonite/gate-indirect-injection-note-body-direct
  gh pr create --base main --head mylonite/gate-indirect-injection-note-body-direct --title 'Mylonite gate: indirect-injection-note-body-direct' --body-file .mylonite/gate/PR_BODY.md

To commit the gate without opening a PR, run the plain command above (no --open-pr), then run only the printed git checkout -b and git add/git commit lines yourself, verbatim — stop before the git push/gh pr create lines. That commits the gate test to a local branch; push and open the PR whenever you're ready, or never.

To do the whole thing — commit, push and open the PR — in one run:

mylonite gate --target-file app.yaml --authorize my-app --open-pr --workflows

--open-pr creates the branch, commits, pushes and opens the PR via gh. --workflows adds the two CI templates: a per-PR gate and a nightly discovery run, each naming the key variable your chosen provider needs. Only a kept finding (step 5's bar) makes it through; a finding that was found but not proven is never silently gated as if it were. See CI gating for the full flow, every flag, and what the PR body carries (the fix, the impact, the evidence, and a reviewer checklist).

Capping the spend. gate runs scan and validate under the hood, so the same --max-llm-calls (per-scan budget) and global --max-llm-requests N / MYLONITE_MAX_LLM_REQUESTS=N (hard ceiling, exits 3) from step 4 apply to the whole gate run.

Exit codes. 9 means at least one proven finding was kept and its gate test written; 0 means the scan ran and found nothing. 10 means nothing was kept, but something reproduced without proof — a candidate, printed with the reason and how to get it proven, never written as a gate test (never-keep-unproven). 5 is a finding that was rejected rather than kept; 6/7 are the generator/validator returning nothing (an internal failure); 8 means the git/gh step itself failed — your findings and validation report are still on disk, not lost.

docs.title: A finding you haven't fixed yet
docs.text: gate commits a test for a weakness that still works on your app as a pending fix, so the PR doesn't turn CI red the day it merges. Step 7 is exactly this: what to run once you've shipped the fix.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: 7. Re-prove — ship the fix, then show it actually worked.

docs.title: 7. Re-prove
docs.text:
You've shipped a fix for the finding step 6 committed. Mylonite doesn't write that fix — it's a change in your own app's code or configuration that closes the gap the gate test proved. This page starts from there, once it's shipped. One local command answers the question the rest of this journey has been building toward: did it actually work?

MYLONITE_LIVE_TARGET=1 pytest .mylonite/gate/

The environment variable is not optional. Without MYLONITE_LIVE_TARGET=1, the test is skipped — every time, before the fix and after it — and pytest exits 0 either way, which looks like a pass but proves nothing. The emitted test is wrapped in a pytest.mark.skipif that pytest evaluates before the test body ever runs, so a bare pytest .mylonite/gate/ never reaches the re-drive, and never reaches @testkit.pending_fix(...) either. mylonite generate/gate print this exact command, with the variable, for that reason.

With MYLONITE_LIVE_TARGET=1 set, this re-drives your real app live: it launches your MCP server and calls the model from step 2 again (testkit.assert_target_resists), so it needs that provider's key and network access to both the provider and your server — the same prerequisites gate itself needed. It is not a replay of recorded fixtures; each run genuinely re-attacks your current build.

This spends too: the global --max-llm-requests N / MYLONITE_MAX_LLM_REQUESTS=N ceiling from step 4 still applies here, since the redrive goes through the same LLM call path.

The committed test also carries @testkit.pending_fix(...), and that decorator is what makes the same command answer "fired before, resisted after" at each stage, with no separate "before" run to remember to keep around:

  1. Before the fix. The attack still lands, so the check fails — reported as an expected failure (xfail), and the run stays green: pytest itself exits 0. This is the "fired before" half: a check that could pass today would be lying about what the pending test is still proving. This is the stage this step's one command reaches if you run it before shipping anything — exit 0 is expected here too, which is why a bare exit-code check alone can't tell "pending, as committed" apart from "actually fixed" (read the printed text either way).
  2. After the fix. The attack lands on no re-drive attempt and is stopped on at least one (3 attempts by default — MYLONITE_REDRIVE_ATTEMPTS=1 makes this a cheaper, single-attempt check; an attempt where the agent made no tool calls counts as neither, and if every attempt is like that the test errors instead), so the check now fails on purpose — a real pytest failure, exit 1 — printing: The attack did not land on any re-drive attempt this run. If your fix has landed, remove the @testkit.pending_fix(...) line above this test. This is the exit code this step expects right after you ship a real fix: 1 here is the "resisted after" half, read as a prompt to act, not a broken build.
  3. Marker removed. Delete the @testkit.pending_fix(...) line. The test is now a plain regression gate: exit 0 while the fix holds, exit 1 if the attack ever works again — the thing CI depends on from here on.

pytest -m mylonite_pending_fix lists every test on your branch still waiting on step 3. The full mechanism — including what counts as "fixed" for a live re-drive, and what a check that never reached a verdict does instead of silently passing — is documented once, in the pending-fix lifecycle and CI gating, including the full cost table; this page exists so the command to run is never more than one page away from "I just fixed it."

docs.title: When you change models instead
docs.text: Re-proving against a new or upgraded model, rather than after a code fix, is a different page: Re-validate on a new model.

docs.title: The habit, from here
docs.text: Steps 1-7 are one pass. Run gate again — on the next change, on a nightly schedule, against the next app you point it at — and each pass adds to the same committed gate directory rather than starting over.

docs.title: Code review — release/0.7.7-honest-results vs main
docs.text: Date: 2026-08-06 Mode: diff (release/0.7.7-honest-results vs main @ 98d1b28) Profile: thorough Verdict: NO-GO as-is, 2 blockers. Both are cheap, targeted fixes (not architectural), and T9 in particular (_redaction.py) is already gated on maintainer sign-off per GOVERNANCE.md — this review's two high findings should be read as required input to that sign-off, not a separate gate. Everything else (0 critical, 13 medium, 4 low) is non-blocking; full test suite (1261 passed, 7 skipped), ruff, mypy, and mkdocs build --strict are all green on the reviewed tip.

docs.title: Coverage
docs.text:
Files in scope 58 changed files (5,947 insertions, 397 deletions) Slices deep-reviewed 26 files / 43 (file, lens) review units across logic/security/performance Slices swept 17 (Haiku triage pass — all clean, none promoted) Slices not reviewed Architecture lens not run this pass (risk-ranked queue for this diff carried no architecture-tagged slices at the thorough cutoff) Findings replayed from ledger 0 (fresh ledger, first run on this branch) Scanners available ruff (0 raw findings — clean) Scanners missing bandit, pip-audit, semgrep, eslint, osv-scanner — coverage gap, notably for a release that includes secret-handling code (T9); nothing installed mid-review per skill rules Parse failures None

State plainly what was not looked at: the docs/ prose diff itself was spot-checked rather than read line-by-line (its factual claims were already independently spec-reviewed twice for T17); this review's code-side scope is cli.py, demo/render.py, and the src//tests/ files listed in the diff. No live-provider/live-target testing was performed (all live e2e tests remain correctly skipped in CI).

docs.title: DCR-0005 — weakness_classes has no membership validation, letting a miscased class silently bypass the W2 seed_arm hard block
docs.text:
• Severity: high (adjudicated: exploitability 2 × impact 3 × exposure 1.0 = 6.0)
  • Standard: logic (general correctness, no CWE mapping)
  • Location: src/mylonite/plugins/_mcp/target_file.py:87 in TargetFile
  • Reachable from: mylonite scan --target-file, mylonite gate --target-file, mylonite validate --target-file — all target-file-driven entrypoints

Failure scenario. A target.yaml with weakness_classes: ["w2"] (lowercase, or any other typo of W2) and no seed_arm passes TargetFile validation — only control_env keys are checked against _WEAKNESS_CLASSES. validate_for_scan's set(tf.weakness_classes) & _INDIRECT_ONLY_WEAKNESS_CLASSES intersection is then empty (case-sensitive), so the hard pre-flight block — which exists specifically to stop a seed-less W2 target from silently reading as clean — never fires, and the scan proceeds without ever planting the indirect-injection payload.

Evidence. 

weakness_classes: list[str] = []

Proposed fix. Add a validator in TargetFile._check (mirroring the existing control_env-key check already present in the same class) that rejects any weakness_classes entry not in _WEAKNESS_CLASSES.

Proof test. Not yet written — recommend tests/plugins/test_target_file.py::test_weakness_classes_rejects_unknown_or_miscased_entry asserting TargetFile(weakness_classes=["w2"]) raises a ValidationError.

docs.title: DCR-0009 — _is_secret_env never checks the key name when the env value is non-string
docs.text:
• Severity: high (adjudicated: exploitability 2 × impact 3 × exposure 1.0 = 6.0)
  • Standard: logic (general correctness, no CWE mapping) — directly material to T9's secret-handling scope
  • Location: src/mylonite/_redaction.py:374 in _is_secret_env
  • Reachable from: redact_target_yaml, called from all three write sites in cli.py (scan scaffold, generate, gate-PR artefact write) — every path that persists a target.yaml copy

Failure scenario. redact_target_yaml on a target.yaml containing env:\n API_TOKEN: 8675309123456 (an unquoted numeric token — YAML parses this as a Python int, not str) hits _is_secret_env's leading isinstance(value, str) check, which returns False before _key_looks_secret(key) is ever evaluated. The key name obviously signals a credential, but the raw numeric value is written verbatim into the persisted .mylonite target.yaml copy — exactly the file this release's ${VAR} indirection work (T9) exists to make safe, and exactly the file the docs tell an operator to commit/push as a gate artefact. The sibling headers masking path is type-agnostic, confirming this is an asymmetry, not a deliberate design choice.

Evidence. 

    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return False
    if _key_looks_secret(key):

Proposed fix. Check _key_looks_secret(key) before the isinstance(value, str) short-circuit, or coerce value to str first so a key-name match still masks a numeric/boolean-typed secret.

Proof test. Not yet written — recommend extending tests/test_redaction.py with test_numeric_valued_secret_key_is_still_masked asserting redact_target_yaml on a YAML doc with env: {API_TOKEN: 8675309123456} produces no occurrence of 8675309123456 in the output.

Escalated: yes, adjudicated by opus → confirmed at high (up from the original reviewer's high, unchanged, but independently re-derived from the rubric rather than taken on trust).

docs.title: Logic
docs.text: ID Severity Location Standard Title DCR-0005 high target_file.py:87 logic weakness_classes unvalidated — see Blockers DCR-0009 high _redaction.py:374 logic _is_secret_env type check ordering — see Blockers DCR-0001 medium cli.py:1081 logic --target-file silently overrides a non-reference: positional TARGET in scan() — the mcp:filesystem-plus---target-file combination scans a different target than the one named on the command line, using the weaker custom-target authorize check instead of the stricter mcp:filesystem one. DCR-0003 medium cli.py:3530 logic Same gap as DCR-0001, in gate() — a pushed gate PR can end up proving a different target than the one named on the command line. DCR-0004 medium cli.py:3604 logic gate()'s scan_fn target_id drops the custom target's scope and diverges from scan()'s report_target_id formula, mislabeling emitted exploit/PR/report artefacts. DCR-0006 medium scan/_llm.py:231 logic _first_balanced_object locks onto the first brace-balanced JSON span in prose-only mode, which can be an earlier draft/example object rather than the model's real final answer — can silently flip a verdict. DCR-0010 medium _redaction.py:190 logic Key-name-based unconditional masking in redact_value only applies to string leaves, not nested list/dict values under a secret-named key — contradicts the docstring's "masked unconditionally" claim. DCR-0011 medium reference_validator.py:1070 logic A vuln_fired=True + guarded-adapter-error combination is mislabeled attack_malformed, contradicting the branch's own comment; misleads debugging of a metamorphic-robustness rejection. DCR-0008 medium _redaction.py:215 logic SecretRedactingFilter.filter's exception guard on a malformed logging call leaves stdlib logging.Handler.handleError() free to print the raw unredacted message to stderr. Adjudicated down from the reviewer's high: transient stderr sink, not a persisted artefact, and requires a separate pre-existing malformed-call bug to trigger. DCR-0012 low reference_validator.py:677 logic Custom-target differential leg's guard_resisted count treats any non-firing guarded run (including adapter errors/timeouts) as genuine resistance, unlike the reference-twin path. Adjudicated down from the reviewer's escalation: fails in the safe direction (routes to a documented fail-closed default), and an identical collapse is already documented as intentional elsewhere in the same module for the same reason. DCR-0007 low test_docs_consistency.py:51 logic Prose-example regex cannot match a mid-string mylonite ... invocation with no trailing ( or em-dash before a newline. Adjudicated: real and reproduced, but bounded — _NEXT_STEP has an explicit count assertion that would catch it; only _TEASER is exposed, and it's test-only code (exposure 0.35).

docs.title: Security
docs.text: ID Severity Location Standard Title DCR-0014 medium _redaction.py:74 V7.1.1 / CWE-532 KV credential regex requires the key immediately adjacent to the separator, so a quoted dict-repr rendering (e.g. str(exc) embedding {'GH_TOKEN': 'ghp_...'}) bypasses redaction entirely. DCR-0015 medium _redaction.py:434 V6.4.1 / CWE-200 redact_target_yaml only masks the headers/request.headers/env sections — a credential embedded in a URL (scheme://<user>:<password>@host) is persisted to git/PR artefacts unredacted, even though _URL_CRED_PATTERN exists elsewhere in the same module to catch exactly this shape.

docs.text: ID Severity Location Standard Title DCR-0016 medium reference_validator.py:422 PERF-SERIAL-IO / CWE-1049 DifferentialValidator's N statistically-independent iterations run sequentially, multiplying wall-clock ~5x at the default iterations=5. Adjudicated down from the reviewer's high: run_twins already parallelizes the two twins within one iteration at max_concurrent=1 as a deliberate throughput/rate-limit boundary, not an oversight — parallelizing further risks provider throttling contaminating the rate statistic the oracle depends on. Still a real, worthwhile optimization (matches the rubric's own N+1 worked example at medium). DCR-0017 medium reference_validator.py:527 PERF-SERIAL-IO / CWE-1049 Custom-target stability re-drives (the n independent live LLM scans in the stability loop) run sequentially. DCR-0018 medium reference_validator.py:620 PERF-SERIAL-IO / CWE-1049 Boundary-guarded-twin differential re-drives are also serialised, doubling the sequential cost on top of the stability loop — up to 2n=10 full LLM-driven scans back-to-back at the default iterations=5. DCR-0019 medium reference_validator.py:1061 PERF-SERIAL-IO / CWE-1049 The 7 built-in metamorphic perturbation strategies are driven through both twins one at a time instead of concurrently. DCR-0020 low reference_validator.py:739 PERF-CACHE Plugin entry-point discovery (discover("mylonite.attack_modules")) is re-run with no caching on every custom-target iteration — up to 10 redundant calls per validate invocation.

docs.title: Cross-cutting themes
docs.text:
1. _redaction.py has three independent gaps in the same release that adds ${VAR} indirection to it (T9). DCR-0009 (non-string value skips key-name check), DCR-0010 (unconditional masking doesn't recurse into lists/dicts), DCR-0014 (quoted-dict-repr bypasses the KV regex), and DCR-0015 (URL-embedded credentials never redacted in redact_target_yaml) are four distinct code paths in the same file that share one root pattern: the module's masking logic was built and tested against the "normal" case (a flat string value under a plain key) and doesn't yet cover the shapes that show up once you go looking for them (non-string YAML values, nested collections, dict reprs, URLs). Given _redaction.py is explicitly gated on maintainer sign-off this release, this cluster is worth reviewing together rather than one finding at a time — fixing DCR-0009 alone without the other three leaves the same "committed copy still leaks in shape X" story just moved to a different shape.
  2. --target-file combined with a non-mcp:custom positional TARGET silently overrides the positional argument, in both scan() (DCR-0001) and gate() (DCR-0003) — the same gap exists at both call sites because both independently re-derive "did the operator mean --target-file or the positional" rather than sharing one resolution function. This is the same class of bug the whole 0.7.7 release exists to close (Class A: fail-opens from re-derived logic instead of a single source of truth) — it just wasn't in the plan's original defect list because it wasn't found until this review.
  3. DifferentialValidator's live re-drive loops (DCR-0016 through DCR-0019) are all the same pattern repeated four times in one class: N or 2N independent, statistically-uncorrelated LLM-driven scans run in a plain sequential Python for/list-append loop instead of a bounded gather. None are individually severe, but together they mean mylonite validate --iterations 5 against a custom target with a guarded adapter costs roughly 5 + 5 + 7 = 17x a single scan's wall-clock instead of something closer to max_concurrent-bounded — worth a single follow-up task consolidating all four into one concurrency-bounded runner rather than four separate point fixes.

docs.title: DCR-0006 — exploit.target_id interpolated raw into generated test docstrings, no validation or escaping
docs.text:
• Severity: critical (adjudicated: exploitability 2 × impact 3 × exposure 1.0 = 6.0 → high, then bumped one band — CWE-94 is on the CWE Top 25 list)
  • Standard: CWE-94 / A03:2021-Injection
  • Location: src/mylonite/plugins/_reference/reference_pytest_generator.py:306 in ReferencePytestGenerator.emit
  • Reachable from: mylonite generate, mylonite gate (which calls generate internally)

Failure scenario. This generator already hardens pattern_id (via _SAFE_PATTERN_ID regex) and control/model/provider (via _py_literal) against exactly this bug — the file's own docstring and DCR history name the """-terminates-the-docstring-and-executes attack these mitigations exist to stop. target_id was missed: it lands bare in the emitted test file's triple-quoted docstrings. target_id is built from an operator- or adapter-supplied family/scope string (TargetFile.family is a bare str with only a 3-name reserved-word validator). If it ever contains a """ sequence, the docstring terminates early and the remainder is interpreted as executable Python the moment pytest collects the emitted, committed test file.

Evidence. 

            target_id=exploit.target_id,

Proposed fix. Validate target_id against a safe-charset regex the same way pattern_id is validated, or render it via _py_literal/_slugify at every docstring interpolation site (module docstring and per-template function docstring), matching the existing treatment of pattern_id/control.

docs.title: DCR-0005 — Raw exception text stored unredacted into ScanAttempt, persisted verbatim to scan_report.json
docs.text:
• Severity: high (adjudicated: exploitability 2 × impact 2 × exposure 1.0 = 4.0)
  • Standard: V7.1.1 / CWE-532
  • Location: src/mylonite/scan/engine.py:522, 806, 844 in ScanEngine._one_pass and sibling call sites
  • Reachable from: mylonite scan, mylonite gate

Failure scenario. verdict_reason=str(exc) is written with no redaction pass at three call sites (adapter/customiser/judge exception handling). write_artefacts persists this verbatim — the project's own code already acknowledges this exposure class (redacting target.yaml before it lands in the scan dir specifically because "request.headers and env may carry live credentials, and the scan dir is one the operator is told to commit"; trimming the generate-dir's copied report for the same reason) but never closed it at the source for exception text. A REST/MCP target whose adapter raises with credential-bearing exception text (an echoed Authorization header, an env-var value in an MCP subprocess launch failure) gets that text written to disk in a directory the CLI's own next-step guidance tells the operator to commit.

Evidence. 

                    verdict_reason=str(exc),

Proposed fix. Route str(exc) through mylonite._redaction.redact() at all three call sites before storing on ScanAttempt, so the persisted artefact is redacted at the source rather than only at console-render time.

docs.title: DCR-0001 — gate silently ignores a bundled mcp:<family> target argument when --target-file (or an auto-discovered mylonite.yaml) is also present
docs.text:
• Severity: high (adjudicated: exploitability 2 × impact 2 × exposure 1.0 = 4.0, promoted from medium)
  • Standard: logic (general correctness, no CWE mapping)
  • Location: src/mylonite/cli.py:3482 in gate, with the trigger broadened by cli.py:3433's mylonite.yaml auto-discovery
  • Reachable from: mylonite gate CLI entrypoint

Failure scenario. if target_file is not None or target == "mcp:custom": short-circuits before target is inspected. Worse than the original report: target_file = target_file or rc.target_file pulls from an auto-discovered mylonite.yaml even with no --target-file flag typed at all — so mylonite gate mcp:filesystem:/scope run in a directory containing a mylonite.yaml with a target_file: entry silently gates the config's target instead, discarding the positional argument with no warning. The reference:* + --target-file collision is rejected loudly a few lines above with an explicit comment; the mcp:* arm has no equivalent guard. The emitted CI gate becomes a false-green for a target that was never actually gated.

Evidence. 

    if target_file is not None or target == "mcp:custom":

Proposed fix. Mirror the existing reference:* + --target-file rejection for any non-mcp:custom target string combined with a resolved target_file (whether from the flag or auto-discovery), so the conflict fails fast instead of silently dropping the positional argument.

docs.text: ID Severity Location Standard Title DCR-0001 high cli.py:3482 logic gate silently ignores a bundled target argument — see Blockers DCR-0002 medium testkit/__init__.py:420 logic Live re-drive filters attack modules to a hardcoded two-id allowlist, excluding a module Mylonite itself ships (reference-indirect-injection) — a committed regression test for an exploit from an unlisted module fails with a misleading "likely a replay/fixture problem" error instead of ever re-driving the target. Fail-closed (no false-green), held at medium rather than promoted. DCR-0003 medium http_adapter.py:143 logic JSON-vs-plain-text template detection keys off adjacent quote characters around {prompt} with no trial-parse (unlike the sibling all-bare-slot branch, which does trial-parse) — a non-JSON template that quotes the slot for prose reasons gets misdetected, and the attack payload is JSON-escaped before substitution into a non-JSON body, corrupting its semantics and risking a false-negative scan result.

Worth a follow-up audit of every .format()/f-string call site in this file for any other unguarded field before the next release touches it again.
  2. The "silently misroutes/misdrops the operator's argument, produces a misleading result instead of a clear error" pattern recurs across two unrelated commands (DCR-0001 in gate, DCR-0002 in testkit's live re-drive) — the exact class of bug the whole 0.7.7→0.7.10 ladder exists to close, just found in new spots this pass. docs.title: DCR-0001 — Scope-required --authorize check vacuously passes when both authorize and scope are None
docs.text:
• Severity: critical (adjudicated: exploitability 3 × impact 2 × exposure 1.0 = 6.0 → high; CWE-863 is CWE Top-25 → mechanically bumped to critical)
  • Standard: CWE-863 (Incorrect Authorization)
  • Location: src/mylonite/cli.py:949 in _build_adapter_for_mcp
  • Reachable from: mylonite scan mcp:<family> (and gate/validate/ablate equivalents) for any family with requires_scope=True, run with no :<scope> segment and no --authorize flag

Failure scenario. Running mylonite scan mcp:filesystem (no :<scope> segment) with no --authorize flag makes authorize != scope evaluate None != None → False, so the explicit-authorization gate silently passes instead of rejecting the missing --authorize. Today the command is only stopped by an unrelated downstream validator — an empty-scope rejection specific to the filesystem/github families — not by this authorization check itself. A future requires_scope=True family whose validator tolerates an empty scope would let an operator launch it with zero --authorize input, bypassing the authorization gate entirely.

Evidence. 

    if spec.requires_scope:
        if authorize != scope:

Proposed fix. Require scope is not None and authorize == scope (or explicitly reject scope is None first) so the authorize gate itself enforces the invariant instead of depending on a downstream, unrelated validator to happen to catch the same case.

Proof test. None generated this pass. Recommend a test_cli.py case that calls _build_adapter_for_mcp (or drives scan mcp:filesystem end-to-end) with authorize=None and no scope segment against a hypothetical/stubbed requires_scope=True family whose validator does not itself reject an empty scope, asserting the authorize gate rejects it directly.

Escalated: yes — adjudicated, exploitability 3 × impact 2 × exposure 1.0 = 6.0 → high, then mechanically bumped to critical (CWE-863, CWE Top-25).

docs.title: DCR-0002 — REST scaffold writes rest_url/rest_body to target.yaml unredacted, unlike the sibling --env path
docs.text:
• Severity: critical (adjudicated: exploitability 3 × impact 3 × exposure 1.0 = 9.0 → critical)
  • Standard: CWE-200 (Exposure of Sensitive Information)
  • Location: src/mylonite/cli.py:3418 in _scaffold_rest_target_file
  • Reachable from: mylonite scan --scaffold --rest-url <url> --output target.yaml (REST scaffold CLI path)

Failure scenario. Operator runs mylonite scan --scaffold --rest-url 'https://api.example.com/chat?api_key=sk_live_abc123' --output target.yaml. The URL — with the live api_key query param, a common real-world credential-in-URL pattern — is written verbatim into target.yaml, and the function's own emitted header text calls the file "runnable as-is" and tells the operator to commit/run it. This persists the credential in cleartext to a file destined for version control, exactly the class of leak already fixed for --env values (via redact_env) in the adjacent MCP-scaffold path, but never applied here.

Evidence. 

request = (RequestSpec(url=rest_url, body=body, response_path=rest_response_path),)

Proposed fix. Apply the same secret-shaped-token redaction used for --env (redact_env) to rest_url and rest_body before writing the scaffold, or strip/mask credential-looking query params and warn the operator to move auth into request.headers as the function's own header comment already recommends.

Proof test. None generated this pass. Recommend a test that scaffolds a REST target with a sentinel api_key=-style query param in --rest-url, asserting the written target.yaml does not contain the sentinel verbatim.

Escalated: yes — adjudicated, exploitability 3 × impact 3 × exposure 1.0 = 9.0 → critical.

docs.title: DCR-0003 — Failed/missing exploit_*.json for a validation artefact silently produces an empty --sarif/--json bundle
docs.text:
• Severity: high (adjudicated: exploitability 3 × impact 2 × exposure 1.0 = 6.0 → high)
  • Standard: internal logic-review checklist (no CWE mapping)
  • Location: src/mylonite/cli.py:3209 in report
  • Reachable from: mylonite report <dir> --sarif out.sarif / --json out.json, any dir holding a validation_report.json with a missing or schema-mismatched exploit_*.json

Failure scenario. Running mylonite report <dir> --sarif out.sarif on a directory holding a validation_report.json but a missing or schema-mismatched exploit_*.json (deleted, or from an older format) hits a load error that is caught and silently swallowed with no warning, leaving dashboard_exploit=None. The findings list becomes empty, so to_sarif/to_bundle writes a zero-result file while the command still prints success and exits 0 — a REJECTED/vulnerable validation shows zero findings in GitHub code scanning with no diagnostic that compliance data was actually missing.

Evidence. 

            except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):
                pass

Proposed fix. On this catch, echo_err a warning that the exploit/compliance file could not be loaded so --sarif/--json output will omit the finding, instead of silently continuing to write an empty bundle.

Proof test. None generated this pass. Recommend a test_cli.py case that runs report --sarif against a directory with a valid validation_report.json but a deliberately corrupted/missing exploit_*.json, asserting the command prints a warning to stderr rather than exiting silently-successful with an empty bundle.

Escalated: yes — adjudicated, exploitability 3 × impact 2 × exposure 1.0 = 6.0 → high.

docs.title: DCR-0004 — Compliance-tag lists are interpolated into generated test docstrings unescaped, unlike every other attacker-influenceable field in this file
docs.text:
• Severity: high (adjudicated: exploitability 3 × impact 3 × exposure 0.35 = 3.15 → medium, cartography-limited exposure; CWE-94 is CWE Top-25 → mechanically bumped to high)
  • Standard: CWE-94 (Code Injection)
  • Location: src/mylonite/plugins/_reference/reference_pytest_generator.py:45 in ReferencePytestGenerator.emit / _fmt_ids
  • Reachable from: every real mylonite generate invocation using the reference pytest generator plugin (no statically-detected entrypoint in this repo's cartography, hence the exposure discount, but this generator runs on the hot path of generate)

Failure scenario. exploit.compliance's tag lists (owasp_llm/owasp_asi/mitre_atlas/nist_ai_rmf) are plain unconstrained list[str] fields with no pattern validator, reachable via the public ExploitRecord passed into emit(). If any entry contains a triple-quote sequence, _fmt_ids joins it unescaped into the module/function docstrings. The triple-quote terminates that docstring early, turning the rest of the emitted test_security_<slug>.py into live top-level Python that executes the next time pytest collects the file — e.g. the committed regression-gate CI run — exactly the injection class this file already fixes for pattern_id/target_id/control via _slugify/_py_literal, but not for the compliance-tag fields.

Evidence. 

Compliance: OWASP LLM {owasp_llm} · OWASP ASI {owasp_asi} · \
MITRE ATLAS {mitre_atlas} · NIST {nist}.

Proposed fix. Validate each ComplianceTags entry against a strict ID charset (like the existing pattern_id validator) at the contract or generator boundary, or route _fmt_ids's output through the same slugify/escape treatment already applied to pattern_id, target_id and control before interpolating into any docstring.

Proof test. None generated this pass. Recommend a tests/plugins/test_reference_pytest_generator.py case that constructs an ExploitRecord with a compliance tag containing """, calls emit(), and asserts the resulting file still parses as valid Python with the docstring intact (or that generation rejects the malformed tag outright).

Escalated: yes — adjudicated, exploitability 3 × impact 3 × exposure 0.35 = 3.15 → medium, then mechanically bumped to high (CWE-94, CWE Top-25).

docs.title: Logic
docs.text:
ID Severity Location Standard Title DCR-0003 high cli.py:3209 logic Missing exploit artefact silently empties --sarif/--json bundle — see Blockers DCR-0005 medium scan/engine.py:737 logic Flakiness-pass semaphore not shared, concurrency scales to max_concurrent² DCR-0006 medium cli.py:2184 logic generate --latest ignores mylonite.yaml's root: key that scan honors DCR-0007 medium cli.py:2627 logic _remediation dict has no metamorphic key DCR-0009 medium cli.py:4248 logic Reference-target DifferentialValidator omits vuln_threshold DCR-0010 medium cli.py:4136 logic LLM-configured check runs after the live adapter is already built DCR-0011 low cli.py:273 logic Dotenv-vs-bare-key detection only inspects the raw first line DCR-0012 low cli.py:484 logic doctor() silently swaps an explicit empty --model for the default DCR-0015 low cli.py:4168 logic target_id resolves inconsistently depending on optional positional arg DCR-0016 low tests/integration/test_custom_target_offline.py:262 logic Real stdio subprocess adapter never closed on any exit path DCR-0018 low scan/engine.py:347 logic Shared consecutive_failures counter misattributes failures under concurrency

DCR-0005 — Per-payload flakiness-pass semaphore is a fresh instance, not the shared cross-payload semaphore, so effective concurrency scales to max_concurrent² instead of max_concurrent

  • Severity: medium (adjudicated: exploitability 3 × impact 2 × exposure 0.35 = 2.1 → medium, cartography-limited exposure — ScanEngine is on the hot path of every real scan/gate/validate/ablate invocation)
  • Standard: internal logic-review checklist (no CWE mapping)
  • Location: src/mylonite/scan/engine.py:737 in ScanEngine._run_flakiness_passes
  • Reachable from: any scan/gate/validate/ablate run with runs > 1 and max_concurrent set

Failure scenario. With ScanConfig(max_concurrent=3, runs=3) and ≥3 applicable payloads: run() builds one outer Semaphore(3) admitting up to 3 concurrent _process_one calls. Each of those, when runs > 1, calls _run_flakiness_passes, which constructs its own new Semaphore(limit) rather than reusing the outer one — so each of the 3 concurrently-processing payloads can itself fan out up to 3 concurrent adapter.invoke() calls, yielding up to 9 simultaneous calls in flight against the target, 3× the configured cap. Confirmed independently by both the logic and performance specialist reviewers on separate passes.

Evidence. 

        limit = max(1, self._config.max_concurrent)
        sem = asyncio.Semaphore(limit)

Proposed fix. Thread the outer semaphore from run()/_process_one down through _run_payload into _run_flakiness_passes instead of constructing a new local one, so total in-flight adapter.invoke() calls never exceed max_concurrent regardless of runs.

Proof test. None generated this pass. Recommend a test that instruments adapter.invoke() to track peak concurrent in-flight calls under max_concurrent=N, runs=M with enough payloads to saturate both, asserting peak concurrency never exceeds N.

Escalated: yes — adjudicated, exploitability 3 × impact 2 × exposure 0.35 = 2.1 → medium. This is a real, independently-double-confirmed correctness bug in a load-bearing safety knob: operators set max_concurrent specifically to avoid overloading rate-limited or subprocess-backed targets.

DCR-0006 — generate --latest silently ignores mylonite.yaml's root: key that scan honors, so it searches the wrong scans directory

  • Severity: medium (non-escalated, high confidence — correctness bug breaking the documented custom-root workflow)
  • Standard: internal logic-review checklist (no CWE mapping)
  • Location: src/mylonite/cli.py:2184 in generate
  • Reachable from: mylonite generate --latest (no --scans-dir) in a directory with a mylonite.yaml setting root:

Failure scenario. With a mylonite.yaml containing root: myroot in the cwd, mylonite scan (no --output-dir) auto-discovers that config and writes artefacts under myroot/scans/<ts>/. mylonite generate --latest (no --scans-dir) instead resolves the layout with no config_root — per the surrounding code's own comment, this path only honors MYLONITE_ROOT/the built-in default since mylonite.yaml's root: key is "unavailable yet at that point" — so generate looks under the default .mylonite/scans and reports "no scans found" even though the scan just ran under myroot/scans.

Evidence. 

    # callback (ctx.obj) — the SAME resolution `scan`'s own default --output-dir
    # uses, so a scan written under a root moved by mylonite.yaml/MYLONITE_ROOT is

Proposed fix. Have generate discover mylonite.yaml (via the same helper scan uses) and pass its root as config_root to the layout resolver, mirroring scan/gate.

Proof test. None generated this pass. Recommend an integration test that writes a mylonite.yaml with a custom root:, runs scan, then runs generate --latest with no --scans-dir, asserting it finds the scan written under the custom root.

Escalated: no (non-escalated, high confidence per the reviewing pass).

DCR-0007 — _remediation dict has no metamorphic key, so a metamorphic-only REJECTED prints no remediation line

  • Severity: medium (non-escalated, high confidence — UX gap in an already-shipped gating path)
  • Standard: internal logic-review checklist (no CWE mapping)
  • Location: src/mylonite/cli.py:2627 in _render_validation_report
  • Reachable from: mylonite validate console rendering, any REJECTED report whose only failing gating leg is metamorphic

Failure scenario. A ValidationReport whose outcomes include stage='metamorphic', passed=False while build/differential/flakiness/etc. all pass, so report.kept=False (metamorphic is a documented gating leg that can cause REJECTED on its own). The REJECTED branch's remediation loop skips the metamorphic outcome because _remediation only keys build/differential/flakiness/stability/effect/consensus — the operator sees "verdict: REJECTED" with zero remediation guidance for the actual failing leg, unlike every other gating stage.

Evidence. 

        _remediation = {
            "build": "build fail: emitted test didn't collect; re-run `mylonite generate`.",
            "differential": diff_remediation,

Proposed fix. Add a "metamorphic" key to the _remediation dict with an actionable message (e.g. naming the failing perturbation strategy).

Proof test. None generated this pass. Recommend a test constructing a ValidationReport with only the metamorphic leg failing, asserting the rendered REJECTED output includes a non-empty remediation line.

Escalated: no (non-escalated, high confidence per the reviewing pass).

DCR-0009 — Reference-target DifferentialValidator omits vuln_threshold that the custom/mcp branch explicitly sets

  • Severity: medium (adjudicated: exploitability 2 × impact 1 × exposure 1.0 = 2.0 → medium)
  • Standard: internal logic-review checklist (no CWE mapping)
  • Location: src/mylonite/cli.py:4248 in gate's validate_fn (reference-target branch)
  • Reachable from: mylonite gate reference:vulnerable --iterations N

Failure scenario. mylonite gate reference:vulnerable --iterations 3 builds its DifferentialValidator with no vuln_threshold argument, while the structurally identical custom/mcp construction 90 lines below explicitly passes vuln_threshold=max(1, iterations - 1) per the documented "all but one" reproducibility rule. The reference path silently falls back to the constructor default instead, so the demo/reference target's pass/fail reproducibility bar is inconsistent with every other target type for no stated reason.

Evidence. 

            validator = DifferentialValidator(
                iterations=iterations,
                provider=effective_provider,

Proposed fix. Pass the same vuln_threshold=max(1, iterations - 1) to the reference-target DifferentialValidator so the documented rule applies uniformly.

Proof test. None generated this pass. Recommend a test asserting both the reference-target and custom-target DifferentialValidator constructions receive the same vuln_threshold for equal --iterations.

Escalated: yes — adjudicated, exploitability 2 × impact 1 × exposure 1.0 = 2.0 → medium.

DCR-0010 — LLM-configured check runs after the live target adapter has already been built, contradicting its own comment

  • Severity: medium (adjudicated: exploitability 2 × impact 1 × exposure 1.0 = 2.0 → medium)
  • Standard: internal logic-review checklist (no CWE mapping)
  • Location: src/mylonite/cli.py:4136 in gate
  • Reachable from: mylonite gate mcp:<family> --authorize <x> with no LLM provider configured

Failure scenario. Running mylonite gate mcp:some-family --authorize me with no LLM provider configured builds the live adapter/subprocess before _require_llm_configured_or_exit runs. The comment states the check runs "BEFORE any adapter/subprocess/engine work starts," but the routed target's adapter is already constructed by the time the check executes, and only then does the command exit on a missing/invalid provider. ablate's equivalent check genuinely precedes all adapter work because it defers adapter construction into a lazily-invoked closure instead of building it eagerly at routing time.

Evidence. 

    _require_llm_configured_or_exit(
        effective_planner_model,
        effective_customiser_model,

Proposed fix. Move the LLM-configured check above the routing/adapter-construction block, or make adapter construction itself lazy (mirroring ablate's deferred closure).

Proof test. None generated this pass. Recommend a test that runs gate mcp:<family> with no provider configured and asserts no subprocess/adapter is spawned before the command exits.

Escalated: yes — adjudicated, exploitability 2 × impact 1 × exposure 1.0 = 2.0 → medium.

docs.text:
ID Severity Location Standard Title DCR-0001 critical cli.py:949 CWE-863 Authorize-vs-scope gate vacuously passes on None == None — see Blockers DCR-0002 critical cli.py:3418 CWE-200 REST scaffold writes credential-bearing URL unredacted — see Blockers DCR-0004 high reference_pytest_generator.py:45 CWE-94 Compliance-tag lists interpolated unescaped into docstrings — see Blockers DCR-0014 low cli.py:1571 CWE-532 Stale comment claims artefacts persist un-redacted — not a live vulnerability, see note below DCR-0017 low scan/engine.py:836 CWE-209 AdapterInvocationSkipped exception text stored unredacted

DCR-0014 — Stale comment above write_artefacts() claims artefacts are persisted un-redacted; the function itself already redacts (fixed in 0.7.9/DCR-0002)

  • Severity: low, scored as informational (1 × 1 × 1.0 = 1.0 → low)
  • Standard: V7.1.1, CWE-532
  • Location: src/mylonite/cli.py:1571 in scan
  • Reachable from: N/A — documentation issue only

This is a documentation issue, not a live vulnerability. It was independently verified by reading scan/artefacts.py's write_artefacts() directly: it already runs the full report/exploit dict through redact_value() before writing, per the 0.7.9 fix (DCR-0002 in the prior review). The comment directly above this call site still says "Persist artefacts UN-redacted... only the console-rendered summary string is redacted," which is now false and misleading to a future maintainer reading this call site — but there is no actual redaction gap here. Flagging this prominently so it is not misread as a third redaction-gap finding alongside the two genuine criticals above.

Evidence. 

        # Persist artefacts UN-redacted (they are loadable/replayable data); only
        # the console-rendered summary string is redacted before display.
        scan_dir = write_artefacts(result, effective_output_dir)

Proposed fix. Update the comment to reflect that write_artefacts() now redacts internally (0.7.9/DCR-0002), so it no longer contradicts the function it describes.

Proof test. N/A — doc-only fix.

Escalated: no (scored informational; explicitly investigated and confirmed not a live gap).

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
ID Severity Location Standard Title DCR-0008 medium cli.py:2650 PERF-SIGNAL-LAT Live provider preflight has no timeout, defeating its own fail-fast purpose DCR-0013 low cli.py:2037 PERF-CACHE target_file re-read and re-redacted from scratch on every finding

DCR-0008 — Live provider reachability probe has no timeout, defeating its own fail-fast purpose

  • Severity: medium (non-escalated, high confidence — availability/hang risk in a CI-facing path)
  • Standard: internal performance-review checklist, PERF-SIGNAL-LAT
  • Location: src/mylonite/cli.py:2650 in _provider_preflight
  • Reachable from: mylonite validate reference-target branch, before the main N-iteration validation loop

Failure scenario. validate's reference-target branch calls _provider_preflight before the real N-iteration validation loop specifically to fail fast rather than burning iterations (per its own docstring). But _provider_preflight neither accepts nor forwards any timeout into engine.run() — if the configured provider accepts the connection but stalls mid-response instead of erroring outright, asyncio.run(engine.run()) blocks indefinitely, hanging the CLI/CI job with no bound. The sibling DifferentialValidator construction 30 lines later explicitly threads iteration_timeout_s into the same kind of live call for exactly this reason — the preflight is the one call in this same code path left unguarded.

Evidence. 

    engine = build_scan(
        "vulnerable",
        completion_fn=None,

Proposed fix. Thread the already-available iteration_timeout (or a default) through _provider_preflight into engine.run() via asyncio.wait_for, so a stalled provider can't hang the CLI before the timeout-guarded validation loop even starts.

Proof test. None generated this pass. Recommend a test that stubs a provider call to hang indefinitely and asserts _provider_preflight returns/raises within a bounded time.

Escalated: no (non-escalated, high confidence per the reviewing pass).

docs.title: Cross-cutting themes
docs.text:
1. Two critical, unrelated findings, not a repeated pattern this time. Unlike 0.7.9's single dominant redaction-gap theme, this release's two critical findings (DCR-0001, the auth-bypass at cli.py:949; DCR-0002, the credential-in-URL leak at cli.py:3418) are independent root causes in independent code paths — one an authorization-logic gate, the other a missing redaction pass on a new scaffold field. Stating this plainly rather than forcing a false unifying narrative.

  2. The 0.7.9 redaction-gap fix is holding up well. Of the ~7 redaction-gap locations fixed in 0.7.9 (DCR-0002/0003/0006/0016/0017/0022/0023 in that report), only one new instance surfaced this release (DCR-0002 here, the REST-scaffold credential-in-URL critical), and one apparent regression (DCR-0014, the stale cli.py comment) turned out to be documentation drift, not a real gap, on direct verification. This is a good signal that the 0.7.9 fix pattern is durable, not that the problem is spreading.

  3. A structural concurrency-budget bug. max_concurrent is silently not enforced when runs > 1 (DCR-0005, the flakiness-pass nested-semaphore finding) — a real, independently-double-confirmed correctness bug in a load-bearing safety knob. Operators set max_concurrent specifically to avoid overloading rate-limited or subprocess-backed targets; this bug lets the effective concurrency reach max_concurrent².

  4. generate/report/gate all share a "silent degrade to less-safe-than-it-looks" pattern this release, in different spots. generate --latest's wrong-directory search (DCR-0006), report --sarif's empty-bundle-on-missing-artefact (DCR-0003), and the metamorphic-remediation-message gap (DCR-0007) all produce a command that exits successfully while quietly doing less than the operator asked for or believes happened. None is individually severe, but as a set it's the same shape of bug repeated three times in this release's diff.

  5. This review's adjudication process caught and corrected itself twice. One finding (a suspected path-traversal via generated.filename) was investigated further and correctly demoted after directly exercising _slugify against the real function — see the note below. A different finding (DCR-0018, the shared concurrent-failure counter) was investigated further and a prior demotion was correctly reversed after the report orchestrator read scan/_llm.py's LiteLLMCallCounter implementation, outside the original reviewer's slice boundary, and confirmed the shared-mutable-counter concern is real. This is stated plainly as evidence the review's confirm/demote step has real teeth in both directions, not just a rubber stamp.

  6. This is the final release of a 4-release remediation ladder (0.7.7 → 0.7.10). The two contract-layer changes in this diff (TestGenerator.emit(exploit, context=None) promoting a metadata shim to a typed parameter, CONTRACT_VERSION 0.1.0 → 0.2.0; ScanReport.aborted retyped from a bare string to an AbortReason-enum-constrained field) and T19's reference-target stdio entry-point work are "closing the loop" items the earlier releases explicitly deferred to this one. Both came back clean at deep-review level — only swept, no findings — so neither is implicated in either critical finding.

Investigated and ruled out (not a finding): a path-traversal concern in _emit_generated_test's test_path = out_dir / generated.filename was flagged by a specialist reviewer at medium/high severity (CWE-22) but demoted after direct verification: running _slugify('../../../etc/passwd') against the real function confirms it maps every non-alphanumeric character (including / and .) to _, so generated.filename can never contain a path separator or .. sequence. Not practically exploitable given the current implementation.

docs.title: Code review — release/0.7.9-any-provider vs 877458a (0.7.8 merge commit)
docs.text: Date: 2026-08-07 Mode: release Profile: economy Verdict: NO-GO — 5 blocking findings (3 critical, 2 high). All 5 sit in one pervasive pattern: sensitive text (LLM provider API keys via a spoofable config, exploit/validation evidence, tool-call output, system-prompt content) that is correctly redacted before console display is written unredacted to disk artefacts or a GitHub API call the CLI's own UX tells the operator to commit or that land in a PR's public Checks tab. This directly contradicts the project's own SECURITY.md/responsible-use posture ("never log payloads containing live secrets"). The new T13–T16 provider-abstraction code itself (model_ref.py, llm_policy.py, schema_sanitise.py, providers.py) is clean — no critical/high findings landed inside it. Additionally flag two medium-severity but headline-relevant regressions before shipping: DCR-0005 undermines this release's own "any provider via --model prefix" pitch, and DCR-0014/DCR-0015 together fully break mylonite gate mcp:<family> (a documented route) whenever a real exploit is found.
